about: Real UK and European families from open-access published case reports, each with a confirmed germline variant (pathogenic or likely pathogenic as reported by the authors; weaker evidence noted in 'notes'), transcribed by AI research agents from the full text and pedigree figures, with quotes in 'evidence' and judgement calls in 'notes'. Citations checked against PubMed on 18 Oct 2026. Kept separate from published-cases.json so each set keeps its own floor; do not tune scoring to individual cases without a source.

cases.variant: c.671-395_2287dup, p.(Ser763Leufs*10) (NM_007294.4), partial exon 10 (legacy exon 11) tandem duplication; reclassified pathogenic (class 5) by authors after RNA analysis
cases.citation: Faversani A et al. Front Oncol 2025;15:1497531
cases.evidence: 'a 50-year-old woman with a personal history of breast cancer'; 'At the age of 49 ... Two lumps ... at the left breast'; 'No Special Type Invasive Carcinoma, Grade 3, Estrogen Receptor 0%, Progesterone Receptor 0% ... HER2 score 0' (second nodule ER 5%); surgical histology 'Estrogen Receptor negative, Progesterone Receptor negative ... HER2 score 0'. 'Her mother had hepatocellular carcinoma and died of it at 64 years old. A maternal aunt was reported to have been diagnosed with gastrointestinal cancer at the age of 80'. 'On the paternal side, the grandmother had colorectal cancer at the age of 70 years, while the father died of an infection at the age of 47'. 'She has two 29-year-old daughters ... cancer-free.' 'we were able to classify the newly identified CNV as pathogenic (Class 5) according to the ClinGen ENIGMA ... Specifications'.
cases.notes: Mother's age at HCC diagnosis not given (died of it at 64), so age left blank. Maternal aunt with 'gastrointestinal cancer' at 80 left out: organ not stated and there is no generic GI code. Second left-breast nodule (ER 5%, grade 3, HER2 0) treated as the same primary (bifocal left breast); ER recorded as negative per the surgical specimen and the paper's 'triple-negative' description. Sister died at 18 of non-cancer causes; father died at 47 of infection; daughters cancer-free (omitted). Variant was VUS on initial testing; no segregation data. Authors note the family history is not suggestive of HBOC.

cases.citation: Larionesi E et al. Discov Oncol 2025;16:1751
cases.evidence: 'A 66-year-old Caucasian male ... presented with progressive right upper limb edema'; 'Family history was significant for breast cancer in two sisters and two brothers, and both parents died of unspecified cancers.' 'Biopsy confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma, grade III, Luminal B HER2-negative (ER+, PR+, HER2 2+, Ki67 25%)'. 'Later CT and colonoscopy revealed a left-sided colonic mass ... moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Post-resection pathology showed pT4aN2b, medullary features, MMR proficient.' 'a heterozygote status of a pathogenic germline BRCA2 variant (c.6275_6276del p. (Leu2092Profs*7))'.
cases.notes: Age at breast diagnosis taken as 66 (age at presentation). Colon cancer age not stated (found 'later', metachronous, presumably about 66) so left blank. HER2 2+ (equivocal, no ISH reported) left unknown although the paper calls it HER2-negative. Siblings' ages at breast cancer diagnosis not given. Both parents 'died of unspecified cancers' – omitted as no site is known.

cases.citation: Blanco A et al. PLoS One 2013;8:e67538
cases.evidence: 'The PALB2 truncating mutation c.1653T>A (p.Tyr551Stop) was identified in a woman diagnosed with an infiltrating ductal carcinoma (IDC), negative for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2 at the age of 36. Her mother had been diagnosed with breast cancer at 48 and with pancreatic cancer at 72 years of age. Her maternal uncle had been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer at 50 years of age (Figure 1A).' Fig 1a pedigree of the c.1653T>A family.
cases.notes: Family A of two PALB2 truncating-variant families in this Spanish series (the second, c.3362del family, not transcribed). Segregation not tested ('not possible to obtain samples from family members'). Pancreatic histology not stated (nos). Current ages/vital status not given in text; pedigree figure not read for further unaffected or deceased status.

cases.variant: Duplication of exons 6-13 (tandem, intron 5 to intron 13 breakpoints; NM_007194.4), paternally inherited; authors consider it pathogenic (reduced mRNA, 'possibly pathogenic' in discussion)
cases.citation: Germani A et al. Diagnostics (Basel) 2022;12:1520
cases.evidence: 'The proband (III:11 Figure 1) was an Italian 48-year-old woman ... She received a diagnosis of invasive lobular carcinoma at age 42 and she reported that her 79-year-old mother (II:6, Figure 1) presented with invasive ductal carcinoma at age 59. She also reported that two paternal aunts (II:3 and II:4) underwent hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for ovarian cancer at age 40.' 'The molecular analysis of first-degree relatives confirmed the inheritance of the variant from the unaffected father (II:5) and showed its presence in the asymptomatic sister (III:10). The duplication was absent in the mother (II:6) ... possible phenocopy.' 'the possible segregation of the variant in the living aunt with ovarian cancer could not be confirmed.'
cases.notes: Mother is a non-carrier (phenocopy) but included because she is part of the reported family history. Unaffected carrier father and sister omitted. Paternal aunts' ovarian histology unknown (nos); one aunt is described as living, the other's status not stated. The authors call the duplication 'possibly pathogenic' in the discussion and show ~44% reduced CHEK2 mRNA (loss of expression from the duplicated allele); included as reported pathogenic finding but this is a judgement call.

cases.variant: c.3747-1G>C (rs730881364), canonical splice acceptor
cases.citation: Lendinez-Sanchez G et al. Case Rep Oncol 2024;17:386-391
cases.evidence: 'a Hispanic woman ... diagnosed in 2015 with 65 years old of localised CM in the right leg'. 'Her family history includes a mother who died probably due to a neoplasia in the head of the pancreas (without pathological confirmation), a son ... diagnosed in 2005, with 24 years old, and localised CM in the left arm ... One of his brothers was diagnosed with ampulloma when he was 53 years old and CM 10 years later, when he was 63 years old.' 'it was tested in the first-degree relatives, resulting positive for ATM c.3747-1G>C; his son was diagnosed with CM at the age of 24. The brother diagnosed with CM when he was 68 years old refused genetic testing.' Málaga, Spain centre.
cases.notes: 'One of his brothers' read as the proband's brother (the next paragraph and discussion call him 'the patient's brother'). Brother's melanoma age given as 63 in one place and 68 in another; 63 used (stated with the 10-year interval). Ampulloma coded as small bowel/duodenum nos (ampullary tumour; malignancy/histology not specified). Mother's pancreatic cancer was 'probable' and unconfirmed by pathology; included with nos histology. Family described as 'Hispanic' but seen in Málaga, Spain; country recorded as Spain. [18 Oct 2026, new form options: brother's ampulloma recoded as ampullary carcinoma.]

cases.variant: c.934C>T, p.(Arg312Trp); functionally deleterious missense (authors)
cases.citation: Gayarre J et al. Br J Cancer 2017;117:1048-1062
cases.evidence: 'the proband, her mother and sister were affected at ages 44 years, 58 years and 45 years by high-grade endometrioid, endometrioid, and undifferentiated ovarian cancer, respectively. A proband's cousin was affected by breast cancer at age 46 years. Other cancers in the family included a gastric carcinoma in the proband's father (at age 81 years) and two colorectal carcinomas in a maternal aunt (at age 71 years) and in a nephew (at age 27 years.) who had been previously diagnosed as a carrier of a de novo APC mutation'. 'All affected members with ovarian cancer were deceased except for the proband.' Variant found in the sister's ovarian tumour (with LOH), absent from the father's normal tissue and gastric tumour, so 'the proband's mother is an obligate carrier'.
cases.notes: Cousin's side and sex not stated in the text (pedigree figure not read) – coded 'other' (side unknown), assumed female. Sister's 'undifferentiated' ovarian carcinoma coded nos. Nephew's colorectal cancer is explained by a de novo APC mutation but included as reported; whose child he is is not stated. Father is a non-carrier; included as reported family history.

cases.variant: c.879delG, p.(Cys294Valfs*16) (NM_002878), novel truncating
cases.citation: Janatova M et al. PLoS One 2015;10:e0127711
cases.evidence: Table 2, patient 1119: 'RAD51D ... c.879delG p.C294Vfs*16 OC (66) n.a. n.a. n.a. D-Thyroid ca (44) & Endometrial ca (44)' (D = daughter; histology, grade, stage not available). Text: 'A novel RAD51D mutation, c.879delG (p.C294Vfs*16), was found in an OC patient with a daughter suffering from BC and OC duplicity.' Truncating mutations described as 'inactivating germline mutations'.
cases.notes: Proband from a series of 171 BRCA1/2-negative high-risk Czech ovarian cancer patients. The daughter's cancers conflict between Table 2 (thyroid and endometrial cancer at 44) and the text (breast and ovarian 'duplicity'); the table was used. Daughter's thyroid cancer left out because its type is not given and there is no unknown-type thyroid code. Ovarian and endometrial histology not available (nos). Daughter's carrier status not reported. No pedigree figure for this family (table data only). [18 Oct 2026: daughter's thyroid cancer added with the new 'type not known' option.]

cases.variant: c.55dup, p.(Tyr19Leufs*2), maternally inherited; proband also carries monoallelic MUTYH c.1187G>A p.(Gly396Asp) from the paternal side
cases.citation: D'Elia G et al. Genes (Basel) 2023;14:428
cases.evidence: 'We describe the case of a 57-year-old woman with BC'. 'The patient was affected with left breast BC at 53 years ... infiltrating ductal carcinoma ... positive for the estrogen receptor (ER 60%), the progesterone receptor (PgR 60%) ... and Her2 (3+).' 'her brother was affected with sarcoma at 11 years of age and died a few months after the diagnosis. The father, who died at 78 years, was affected with CC, diagnosed at 63 years. Moreover, two paternal uncles, both dead, were affected by CC developed at 60 and 74 years respectively. In addition, a paternal aunt developed gastric cancer (GC) at 72 years, and a paternal cousin, 38 years old, was affected with BC diagnosed at 38 years. On the maternal side, two uncles, 78 and 85 years of age, were affected with BC diagnosed at 53 and 60 years, respectively.' 'the same BRIP1 mutation in the healthy mother of 83 years, and the same MUTYH mutation in the paternal cousin with BC.'
cases.notes: Dual finding: the authors attribute the paternal-side cancers (colorectal, gastric, cousin's breast) to the monoallelic MUTYH variant and the maternal-side cancers (two male breast cancers) to BRIP1; the brother's sarcoma side is uncertain. Gene recorded as BRIP1 per assignment, but the family is mixed. Brother's sarcoma type not stated – coded 'other soft tissue sarcoma' (could be bone). Maternal 'uncles' with breast cancer taken as male as written. Unaffected carrier mother omitted. [18 Oct 2026, new form options: brother's sarcoma of unstated type recoded "type not known".]

cases.variant: Heterozygous deletion of exons 8-11 (NM_000465.2), maternally inherited
cases.citation: Carrera S et al. Hered Cancer Clin Pract 2023;21:2
cases.evidence: 'a 49-year-old Caucasian man ... a tumor in the middle rectum. The biopsy was compatible with an intestinal adenocarcinoma and immunohistochemistry (IHC) for MMR proteins was proficient (pMMR)'; MSI 'stable (MSS)'. 'he had a 60-year-old sister who was diagnosed with pMMR endometrial adenocarcinoma at the age of 56. His 86 year old father was diagnosed at the age of 85 with colon adenocarcinoma with loss of MLH1-PMS2 in the IHC, BRAF V600E wild-type (WT) and hypermethylation of the MLH1 promoter ... His mother, who was diagnosed with colon cancer at the age of 53, died at the age of 55. One of his maternal aunts died of colon cancer at the age of 50 ... another maternal aunt died at age 80 and had triple negative breast cancer at age 74, and his maternal uncle died at age 81 and was diagnosed with colon cancer at age 79. His maternal grandmother died at 60 from a probable cancer of unknown origin'. Sister carrier; father non-carrier; mother, maternal uncle and TNBC aunt obligate carriers.
cases.notes: Maternal aunt who died of colon cancer at 50: age at diagnosis not given (blank, ageDeath 50). Maternal grandmother's 'probable cancer of unknown origin' (died 60) left out – no site. Sister's endometrial adenocarcinoma subtype not stated (nos). Father is a non-carrier with a likely sporadic MLH1-methylated colon cancer; included as reported. Proband's current age not given.

cases.variant: c.376-2A>G (NM_000546.6), likely pathogenic (class 4)
cases.citation: Stojiljkovic D et al. Case Rep Oncol Med 2024;2024:6699698
cases.evidence: 'In September 2005, at the age of 17 ... large left breast tumor ... Phyllode glandulae mammae'; timeline: 'pathohistology report confirmed it was malignant tumor'. 'December 2007 ... tested positive for pheochromocytoma, and underwent a right-sided adrenalectomy.' 'In December 2014 ... rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor (RGNT).' '2016/2017 ... confirmed an adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC)' (2017). 'May 2020 ... type B2 thymoma.' 'In November 2021 ... right breast ... invasive ductal carcinoma'; Fig 3 'breast ductal carcinoma: (a) HER2+, (b) ER+, and (c) PR+'. 'the mother was diagnosed with bilateral breast cancer (age 28 and age 48) and the grandmother was diagnosed with the breast cancer at the age of 36'. 'six primary tumors by the age of 33 years'.
cases.notes: Ages derived from dates (age 17 in Sept 2005): phaeochromocytoma Dec 2007 ~19, RGNT Dec 2014 ~26, ACC 2017 ~29, IDC Nov 2021 ~33. RGNT (WHO grade 1 glioneuronal tumour) coded as low-grade glioma (closest code). Thymoma (B2) at ~32 left out – no code. Phyllodes coded malignant per the timeline. Grandmother's side not stated (pedigree figure not read) – coded 'other'. Mother's carrier status not reported. ARMC5 variant also reported (adrenal macronodular hyperplasia). Proband's current age not stated.

cases.variant: MLH1 LRG_216t1:c.2236_2247delCTGCCTGATCTA p.(Leu746_Leu749del), in-frame deletion; classified likely pathogenic by authors (ACMG PM1, PM2, PM4, PP1-moderate)
cases.citation: Klančar G et al. Genes (Basel) 2020;11(3):325
cases.evidence: 'The proband (III-1) was first seen at our Cancer Genetics Clinic with the diagnosis of carcinoma of the caecum at the age of 39 ... poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (stage pT3N2M0).' 'The proband's mother (II-5) developed adenocarcinoma of the ileal flexure aged 41 and an EC aged 50. Her brother (II-6) (proband's uncle) developed a carcinoma of the caecum aged 29 and died a year later, at the age of 30. Her mother (I-4) (proband's grandmother) had been treated for ovarian cancer at the age of 43 and carcinoma of the caecum aged 57. She died at the age of 58. The grandmother's brother (I-5) (proband's great uncle) developed a rectal carcinoma at the advanced age of 85.' 'On the proband's father's side of the family only squamous cell skin cancers were reported.' 'All carrier's tumor samples (III-1, II-5, and II-6) lacked the expression of PMS2 protein and had MSI-H status'; Table 1: MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 retained in proband's caecal tumour, PMS2 0%. 'Non-carriers of the variant (III-2 and I-5) had normal expression of all MMR proteins ... and MSI-S status.'
cases.notes: IHC showed isolated PMS2 loss (MLH1 retained) in all carriers' tumours, recorded as 'pms2' exactly as reported even though the germline gene is MLH1 (the paper's main point). For the mother's endometrial cancer MLH1 staining was technically inadequate and PMS2 was lost; recorded as 'pms2'. The mother's 'adenocarcinoma of the ileal flexure' (Table 1 lists the sample as 'ileum') is recorded as colorectal; it could be read as small bowel. Grandmother's ovarian cancer age is 43 in the case description and 42 in the discussion; 43 used. Great-uncle (I-5) is the grandmother's brother, so maternal great-uncle; he tested negative (FFPE) with an MSS, MMR-intact rectal cancer at 85 (86 in the discussion) — a phenocopy, kept because he would appear in the family history. Unspecified paternal relatives with cutaneous SCC left out (no individuals or ages given). Proband's current age not stated. Unaffected non-carrier sister left out.

cases.variant: MSH2 heterozygous deletion of exons 1-3 (MLPA), reported as pathogenic
cases.citation: Challis BG et al. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;101(6):2269-72
cases.evidence: 'In 2001, the proband (patient III:2), a 54-year old female presented ... She had previously undergone a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for ovarian cancer at age 44 years and endoscopic removal of a malignant colonic polyp at age 47 years.' Right adrenal mass: 'in keeping with an oncocytic AAC based on Lin-Weiss-Bisceglia criteria'. 'The proband's sister (patient III:1) ... at age 36 years ... was diagnosed with an adenocarcinoma of the descending colon ... At age 47 years, she was diagnosed with endometrial carcinoma'. 'the proband's maternal aunt (patient II:3) and grandfather (patient I:1) had both been diagnosed with colorectal cancer (Figure 1). Importantly, the certificate of death for the proband's mother (patient II:2) stated metastatic ACC as the cause of death.' 'In all analyzed tumors [both ACCs and the sister's endometrial tumour], expression of MLH1 and PMS2 was retained, whereas nuclear staining for MSH2 and MSH6 were absent'. MLPA: 'heterozygous deletion of exons 1, 2, and 3 of the MSH2 gene' in proband and sister. Fig 1: I:1, II:2, II:3 shown deceased.
cases.notes: Authors from Cambridge and Edinburgh (UK). MSH2/MSH6 loss in both ACCs is not recorded because the adrenal site has no MMR marker field; recorded for the sister's endometrial cancer only. Proband's 'malignant colonic polyp' at 47 recorded as colorectal cancer, histology unspecified. Ovarian histology not given. Ages for mother's ACC, aunt's and grandfather's CRC not given; deceased status from pedigree slashes. TP53 testing negative in proband. Carrier children and niece are unaffected and omitted.

cases.variant: MSH6 NM_000179.3:c.2726_2727ins[SVA[3293];2713_2726] (SINE-VNTR-Alu retrotransposon insertion in exon 4), reported by authors as the causative germline variant
cases.citation: Sjursen W et al. Hered Cancer Clin Pract 2025;23(1):22
cases.evidence: 'Two siblings, one male (Fig. 1, II:2) and one female (Fig. 1, II:5), were suspected to have a hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome ... The male patient had been diagnosed with a papillary urothelial carcinoma in the bladder at 77 years of age. He was then treated for colon cancer at age 78. Finally, rectal cancer was discovered at age 84. His sister had developed several cancers at an earlier age. She was treated for ovarian cancer at age 36. Later, she was diagnosed with ureteral cancer at age 57 and then colorectal cancer at age 60. In addition, the daughter of the male patient was diagnosed with ovarian cancer at age 46.' 'No pathogenic variant was detected before the two siblings passed away.' 'IHC showed missing protein staining for MSH2 and MSH6 in one tumor, and MSH6 in two tumors. All three tumors showed microsatellite instability.' Fig 1 (yellow = colon polyps): III:9 (II:5's daughter, carrier) and III:3, III:5 (II:2's sons, non-carriers) have colon polyps. 'only family members with the SVA insertion in MSH6 developed cancer.'
cases.notes: Both siblings are marked as index cases; the sister (II:5) is used as proband because she had the earlier-onset cancers. 'Ovarian cancer' histology not given. MMR IHC/MSI results were not attributed to individual tumours, so not recorded. Polyp histology, counts and ages not given ('benign colon polyps'); the two nephews with polyps tested negative for the insertion (phenocopies) but are kept as reported in the pedigree; they are coded 'niece' (niece/nephew). Earlier-identified MSH2 c.815C>T and MSH6 c.1720T>A are benign/likely benign. Ages at death not given.

cases.variant: Biallelic PMS2 c.[137G>T];[(2174+1_2175-1)_(*160_?)del] p.(Ser46Ile) (class 4) / deletion of exons 13-15 (class 5) - constitutional mismatch repair deficiency
cases.citation: Pedroni M et al. Genes (Basel) 2022;13(11):1953
cases.evidence: 'At age 10, rectal bleeding was noted. A first colonoscopy (1992) identified the presence of eight polyps (adenomatous at histology)'. 'In 2007 (age 25), a colonoscopy showed more than 20 lesions ... In one of these polyps (in the sigmoid), features of adenocarcinoma'; 'the resected carcinoma showed an elevated microsatellite instability with all markers, together with altered expression of the MLH1 protein ... PMS2 not tested'. 'In 2012 (age 30) ... an infiltrating adenocarcinoma was detected with a transmural extension through the ileal wall (T4N0Mx).' 'In 2016 (age 34) ... a well-differentiated duodenal adenocarcinoma (T3N0Mx).' 'December 2017 (age 35) ... definitive diagnosis of lymphoblastic lymphoma.' 'The proband's brother, born in 1986, died at age three (1989) of lymphoblastic leukemia.' Table 1B: Jejunum (2012) PMS2 and MLH1 not expressed; Duodenum (2016) PMS2 not expressed, MLH1/MSH2/MSH6 expressed. 'The proband is a 40-year-old man'. Parents (monoallelic carriers) unaffected with normal colonoscopies around 50.
cases.notes: CMMRD family (both parents heterozygous carriers, unaffected). The proband also carries class 3 VUS in APC, MSH2 and CHEK2. 'Multiple freckles and several hyperpigmented spots on the thorax' were described but not stated to be café-au-lait macules (>=6), so 'cal' not recorded. Colorectal cancer IHC showed MLH1 'altered' with PMS2 not tested (authors suspect artefact) and MSI-H, recorded as 'msi'. The 2012 small-bowel cancer is described as ileal in the text but as 'Jejunum (2012)' in Table 1B, where MLH1 and PMS2 were both not expressed — recorded literally as 'mlh1'. Polyp count at 10 is 8 adenomas; later >20 lesions. Brother's leukaemia recorded as ALL (lymphoblastic). Sister has sarcoidosis (no code); omitted.

cases.variant: APC NM_000038.5:c.4609dup p.(Thr1537Asnfs*7), novel frameshift, classified pathogenic
cases.citation: Antohi C et al. Diagnostics (Basel) 2021;11(9):1560
cases.evidence: 'The proband is a young Caucasian female (16 year old at the time of diagnosis). She was referred to an oral surgeon because of a mandibular osteoma ... The proband's brother (12 year old at the time) had supernumerary teeth and a mandibular tumor on palpation. Family history showed that the proband's mother was diagnosed with mandibular osteoma, supernumerary teeth and died at 34 years old because of intra-abdominal and abdominal wall tumors. The maternal grandfather had supernumerary teeth and soft tissue tumors and died around the age of 35'. CBCT of both siblings: multiple osteomas of skull, jaw and sinuses; impacted teeth. Proband: 'Lower digestive endoscopy revealed multiple polyps (approximately 50-70)' - 'tubular adenomatous polyp with low-grade epithelial dysplasia'. Both siblings carry APC c.4609dup.
cases.notes: Mother's 'intra-abdominal and abdominal wall tumors' and grandfather's 'soft tissue tumors' are probably desmoids but the paper does not say so, so they are not coded. The grandfather is coded with 'osteomas' (multiple osteomas / dental anomalies) for supernumerary teeth only. Polyp count 50-70, recorded as 50; age at colonoscopy not stated (after diagnosis at 16; osteoma removal at 18). Brother's breast lipoma not coded. Abstract and text mention 'family history of colon cancer' generically but no relative with colorectal cancer is described, so none entered.

cases.variant: MUTYH c.1187G>A p.(Gly396Asp) homozygous (biallelic), pathogenic
cases.citation: Fabišíková K et al. Front Genet 2020;11:590486
cases.evidence: Case 1: 'The proband was a 67-year-old woman presenting with a personal history of CRC diagnosed at the age of 54 and endometrial cancer diagnosed at the age of 65. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated intact expression of MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2. Colorectal tumor that developed was microsatellite stable.' 'The grandmother of the patient developed breast cancer at the age of 48. The brother of the proband died aged 50 from an unknown gastrointestinal disease (probably gastric cancer; Figure 1).' 'A panel of 26 cancer predisposition genes identified a germline homozygous (biallelic) pathogenic variant c.1187G > A (p.Gly396Asp)'. Fig 1: grandmother (CAMA 48) is the mother's mother; brother 'GASTRIC DISEASE 50', deceased.
cases.notes: Case 1 of a two-case report (case 2 involves only monoallelic carriers and is not used). No polyp count is given for the proband (atypical presentation without reported polyposis). Brother's 'unknown gastrointestinal disease (probably gastric cancer)' not entered because cancer is not confirmed. Grandmother placed as maternal from the pedigree. PALB2 c.229T>C and a TP53 intronic variant are VUS. Three unaffected heterozygous children omitted.

cases.variant: POLE NM_006231.2:c.1089C>A p.(Asn363Lys), exonuclease domain, segregating in 12 carriers; reported as the disease-causing mutation
cases.citation: Rohlin A et al. Int J Oncol 2014;45(1):77-81
cases.evidence: 'Family member III:4 (Fig. 1) had a prophylactic colectomy with ileo-rectal anastomosis (IRA) at 47 years with an accidental unexpected finding of CRC. She also developed a malign rectal tumour at 53 years. Two affected individuals in the family, I:1 and III:10 developed primary brain tumours, a glioma in one case and a giant cell glioblastoma in the other.' 'a mutation carrier also developed pancreatic cancer at age 78 (Fig. 1, family member II:9).' 'family member III:7 with gastric cancer could not be tested'. Fig 1 pedigree: I:1 CRC 65, brain tumor 68 (glioma); II:2 CRC 43, ovarian ca 50, endometrial ca 50; II:4 CRC 56; II:7 CRC 28; II:9 ovarian ca 45, CRC 52 and 78, pancreatic ca 78; II:11 ovarian ca 45, endometrial ca 45; III:2 CRC 35; III:6 CRC 55; III:7 gastric ca 43; III:9 CRC 40; III:10 brain tumor 28 (giant cell glioblastoma); IV:2 CRC 38; IV:3 adenomas 28. 'Five colorectal tumours from three affected individuals were all microsatellite stable (MSS)'.
cases.notes: No proband is marked; III:4 (first described, exome-sequenced) is used. Relationships derived from Fig 1: II:2 is her mother, I:1 her maternal grandmother, II:4/II:7/II:9/II:11 her mother's siblings, III:6/III:7/III:9/III:10 maternal first cousins, IV:2/IV:3 her brother III:2's sons. Deceased status read from pedigree slash marks; ages at death not given. The grandmother's 'glioma' grade is not stated; the cns site has no unspecified code, so it is entered as 'hgg' (forced choice) - the cousin's giant cell glioblastoma is a true hgg. Pancreatic and gastric histology not given. MSS results were not attributed to individuals, so not recorded. Carriers had a limited number of adenomas (AFAP/MAP range) but counts were not given. [18 Oct 2026: grandmother's glioma of unstated grade recoded as the new 'Glioma – grade not known' option.]

cases.variant: NTHL1 NM_002528.7:c.[244C>T];[435_446del] p.[(Gln82Ter)];[(Leu146_Arg149del)] - compound heterozygous; c.435_446del novel, classified likely pathogenic by authors
cases.citation: Pinto C et al. Front Genet 2023;14:1254908
cases.evidence: Family 3: 'Patient #5 ... was a woman diagnosed with five polyps and rectal cancer at 52 years, bilateral BC at 54 and 58 years and uterine carcinosarcoma at 58 years. She had two brothers with biallelic variants (relatives #3 and #4), one diagnosed with two synchronous CRCs and polyposis (15-20 polyps) at 62 years old and another diagnosed with polyposis at 50 years old and a basal cell carcinoma (Figure 1C).' 'The variant NM_002528.7:c.435_446del ... is here classified as likely pathogenic following the ACMG guidelines'. Fig 1C: patient #5 age 60; relative #3 age 62; relative #4 age 56 ('Polyposis 50, Skin'); mother (deceased) 'Breast 88' with '84' beneath the symbol; father deceased at 93.
cases.notes: Index patient #5 of family 3 (the study also reports two other biallelic families). Polyp histology not stated for any of the three, so 'nos' used; brother #3 count 15-20 recorded as 15; brother #4 count not given. 'Rectal cancer' recorded as colorectal; histology not given. Mother's breast cancer: the pedigree shows 'Breast 88' but also the number 84 (presumably age at death), which conflict; age left blank. Three healthy siblings (two in-frame-variant carriers, one negative) omitted.

cases.variant: SMAD4 NM_005359.6:c.386A>C p.(Asn129Thr), mosaic in proband (AF 22%), heterozygous in son; classified likely pathogenic by authors
cases.citation: Valentín F et al. Mol Genet Genomic Med 2024;12(1):e2348
cases.evidence: 'A 46-year-old male with no family history of cancer and chronic iron deficiency anemia ... diagnosed with massive gastric polyposis (>=100 polyps). Biopsies revealed hyperplastic inflammatory polyps'. 'for the last 14 years, he has undergone surveillance colonoscopies with the removal of multiple polyps throughout the colon (16 adenomatous, 4 hamartomatous, and 19 inflammatory polyps), therefore, meeting diagnostic criteria for JPS'. 'at the age of 59 ... total gastrectomy ... a 5 cm gastric hyperplasic polyp with high-grade dysplasia and focal adenocarcinoma.' 'One son of the CI aged 30 years was diagnosed as a SMAD4 c.386A>C p.(Asn129Thr) carrier. Gastroenterological examination revealed two subcentimeter polyps in the colon and seven inflammatory gastric polyps'. No telangiectasia or AVMs on screening.
cases.notes: Mosaic de novo variant (absent in both parents) - atypical presentation. Colonic polyps were mixed (16 adenomatous, 4 hamartomatous, 19 inflammatory over 14 years), coded 'mixed' count 39, age not given; gastric polyposis (>=100 hyperplastic/inflammatory) coded as polyps 'nos' count 100 at 46 because there is no gastric-polyp code. Gastric cancer recorded with histology 'nos' (focal adenocarcinoma in a hyperplastic polyp). Proband current age not stated (seen 12 months after surgery at 59). Pathological diagnosis: 'Pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma in an intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm.'
cases.notes: Relatives are not described individually (only 'from a kindred with FAMMM'), so only the proband is entered. Adenosquamous carcinoma is a variant of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, so coded pdac. Age at melanoma not given (resected in 1997, roughly 19-20 years before presentation, not stated). cases.citation: Martino S et al. Front Oncol 2024;14:1419739

'The daughter (IV-3), 32 years old, is the sole family member who tested positive ... underwent exportation of two basal cell carcinoma after the test.'
cases.notes: Relationships and ages read from the pedigree figure (small image). The legend lists lung cancer in III-11 but the figure shows lung cancer in II-11 (maternal uncle) and thyroid/melanoma in III-11; I followed the figure. The proband's melanoma at 56 was a spinal metastasis from an unknown primary; entered as a second melanoma diagnosis. GIST location given as 'left colon' in the text and 'right colon' in Table 1. Thyroid cancer histology not stated for sister and paternal cousin ('papillary' is a placeholder; thyroid has no 'nos' code). Segregation testing covered the father, daughter and son, and the daughter is 'the sole family member who tested positive', so the father (melanoma at 90) is a non-carrier (phenocopy); the variant presumably came through the mother (not tested). [18 Oct 2026: the sister's and paternal cousin's thyroid cancers (placeholder papillary) recoded as the new 'type not known' option.]

cases.variant: Heterozygous deletion of NF2 5'UTR and exon 1 (NM_000268.3) by MLPA, pathogenic
cases.citation: Ognibene M et al. Int J Mol Sci 2025;26(14):6848
cases.evidence: 'A one-year-old boy was diagnosed with severe NF2-related schwannomatosis and treated with several neurosurgical exereses (cerebral and spinal meningiomas and vestibular schwannomas)'. 'overall survival of about one year; then the patient died because of rapidly increasing meningiomas'. 'there was no tumor family history and no environmental exposure to asbestos'. 'a heterozygous deletion of the NF2 gene ... encompassing the 5'UTR ... and exon 1'.
cases.notes: Single proband with no family history (likely de novo), included as a characteristic NF2 presentation with an atypical cancer (childhood pleural mesothelioma, with somatic loss of the second NF2 allele). Ages at the individual meningiomas and vestibular schwannomas are not given (NF2 diagnosed at age 1), so left blank. Mesothelioma age 13 from 'at the age of 13, developed a PM'. cases.variant: c.122A>T (creates a new exonic 5' donor splice site; 84 bp loss from exon 2 on RNA), reported as pathogenic
cases.citation: Setrajcic Dragos V et al. Front Genet 2019;10:762
cases.evidence: Patient 1: 'referred to our cancer genetics clinic at the age of 54 ... The patient developed a hormone-positive, Her-2-negative breast cancer aged 47.' 'At age 48, she was diagnosed with an ovarian tumor, which proved to be a mucinous cystadenoma'. 'she had less than six café-au-lait spots. In addition, axillary freckling was observed. Breast histology not stated; 'hormone-positive' entered as ER positive (PR not separately stated). Father's oropharyngeal carcinoma coded headneck scc as a placeholder (histology not stated; headneck has only an scc code). Paternal grandmother's 'uterine carcinoma' coded uterus nos. No ages for relatives. Mother possibly affected with NF1 skin signs (not tested) – not coded. Benign mucinous cystadenoma not coded. ageNow 55 is the latest age mentioned (haemothorax at 55). [18 Oct 2026, new form options: father's oropharyngeal cancer of unstated histology recoded "type not known".]

'Later, the patient presented jaw keratocystic odontogenic tumors (KCOTs)'. 'multiple histologically proven odontogenic keratocysts occurred before the age of 20'. cases.variant: Germline SVA-E retrotransposon insertion in SMARCB1 intron 2 disrupting splicing (loss of function); inherited from a mosaic mother
cases.citation: Sabatella M et al. J Pathol 2021;255(2):202-211
cases.evidence: 'The first daughter (II-1) of a healthy Dutch couple was diagnosed with ATRT at birth, with negative immunohistochemical staining for SMARCB1'. 'a few years later, a second daughter (II-2) was also born with congenital ATRT, again negative for SMARCB1 immunostaining'. 'Both tumors were classified as ATRT-SHH subtype through methylome profiling'. 'two siblings with congenital ATRT due to a germline SVA-E retrotransposon insertion into intron 2 of the SMARCB1 allele'; 'the mother is a mosaic carrier'.

cases.variant: Heterozygous deletion of WT1 exon 8 and exons 9-10 (NGS)
cases.citation: Rdzanek O et al. Appl Clin Genet 2024;17:199-203

Examination: 'absence of testes in the scrotum'. 'Imaging ... revealed the presence of pathological tissue changes in both kidneys. Based on this, stage V Wilms' tumor was diagnosed.' Right kidney: 'nephroblastoma, predominantly stromal type'. 'Genetic testing revealed a deletion fragment of exon 8 and exons 9–10 on one allele of the WT1 gene.'
cases.notes: Bilateral Wilms tumour (stage V) at about 2.5 years entered as age 2. Undescended testes coded feature gu_anom. cases.variant: c.3712G>A p.(Val1238Ile), germline (authors: germline MET mutation causing HPRCC)
cases.citation: Ferlicot S et al. Diagn Pathol 2021;16(1):107
cases.evidence: 'The patient, a 51-year-old man, without a familial background of RCC, underwent computed tomography for hypertension investigation that revealed bilateral and multifocal renal tumors.' Eight left and five right tumorectomies: 'Three nodules ... had typical histological features of clear cell RCC with ISUP grade 1 ... The other nodules showed typical histological features of papillary tumors, either type 1 papillary RCC (5 tumors) or papillary adenomas'. 'on peripheral blood testing, a germline MET mutation c.3712G>A, p.(Val1238Ile) was found, but no VHL germline mutation.' Later 'left adrenalectomy for RCC metastasis' (clear cell).
cases.notes: Single proband with no family history of RCC, included because bilateral multifocal type 1 papillary RCC is characteristic of HPRCC; the co-existing clear cell RCCs make it atypical (FLCN tested first, negative). Both kidney entries at 51 (age at first imaging; right kidney tumours resected two years later). The authors call it a 'germline MET mutation' but give no ACMG class; this is the case they present as HPRCC. Adrenal metastasis not coded as a separate primary.

cases.variant: c.1372G>T p.(Glu458*) (NM_016222.2), likely pathogenic (class 4, PVS1+PM2) per authors; co-segregating with two VUS c.404G>T and c.1046T>C in some siblings
cases.citation: Wagner JN et al. Biomedicines 2023;12(1):64
cases.evidence: 'A 64-year-old man presented with an initial diagnosis of AML.' 'The family history revealed that the patient's brother and father had hematologic neoplasms. The brother was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia in 2017, which progressed from a previously diagnosed myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS).' 'Next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis of a stored DNA sample confirmed the DDX41 mutation. Another affected brother is currently diseased with a clear-cell renal cell tumor, and the father had suffered from chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)'. 'both parents are already deceased'. 'The DDX41 variant c.1372G>T leads to ... [p.(Glu458*)] ... assessed as probably disease-relevant (IARC class 4) according to the ACMG evaluation criteria (criteria applied: PVS1, PM2).' Fig 3 pedigree: father CLL (deceased); proband AML; brother sAML; brother clear-cell RCC (carrier dot); three sisters DDX41 mut. (unaffected); one brother and proband's daughter DDX41 neg.

cases.variant: c.350del p.(Gly117Alafs*43), pathogenic (class 5)
cases.citation: Demaret T et al. Front Genet 2025;16:1575651
cases.evidence: 'Aged 41, the proband presented with 3 synchronous tumors ... A tubulovillous adenoma (high-grade dysplasia) of the right colic flexure, associated with multiple colon polyps (low-grade dysplasia), and an unclassified renal cell carcinoma were resected ... the patient declined the resection of a hypermetabolic nodule located inside a nodular goiter'. 'His medical history was marked by an AML, at the age of 9'; HSCT at 12 from his older sister. 'He further developed bilateral cataracts (surgically corrected at 26 years)'; 'progeroid appearance ... premature graying of hair ... prematurely aged face, and short stature'. 'Their two eldest children died of AML at the ages of 38 years (AML diagnosed at 37) and 34 years (AML diagnosed at 12) ... The oldest of the two was the donor for the proband's HSCT. She had 3 children, two of whom developed AML before the age of 18.' 'A heterozygous c.350del p.(Gly117Alafs*43) pathogenic variant in the CEBPA gene was found in the proband's urine and blood DNA, and in his affected relatives.' Fig 1B: II.1 female deceased AML; II.2 male deceased AML; II.4 proband; III.1, III.2 (daughters of II.1) AML. Fig 1A timeline: III.1 and III.2 first AML at ~16-17 y.

Proband's colon lesions coded as polyps/adenoma (tubulovillous adenoma with HGD plus multiple polyps; count not given) rather than colorectal cancer. RCC 'unclassified' -> kidney/nos. Thyroid hypermetabolic nodule in a nodular goitre was not resected -> thyroid/mng (no cancer diagnosis). Progeroid features/early cataracts coded as feature/progeroid because reported, although the authors attribute them to AML treatment (phenocopy of Werner syndrome; WRN not confirmed). Proband's ageNow taken as 41 (age at presentation). De novo/parental mosaic: mother tested negative; father deceased of non-malignant cause at 66, omitted. cases.variant: c.1163T>C p.(Met388Thr), germline, segregating in four relatives with GATA2 deficiency (authors do not state an ACMG class)
cases.citation: Romero-Moya D et al. Leukemia 2025;39(4):962-966
cases.evidence: 'This three-generation GATA2 family presented four members with identical germline GATA2 mutations (p. Met388Thr; c.1163T>C) and variable clinical manifestations.' 'Patient #3 (P3) is a female diagnosed with pancytopenia at age 29 ... Her medical history includes Mycobacterium avium infection, thrombocytopenia, obstetric complications, and an arterial aneurysm. At age 31, she was diagnosed with MonoMac syndrome ... (monocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and anemia) ... lack of NK cells ... Bone marrow (BM) analysis revealed MDS with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD) and trisomy 8'. 'Patient #4 (P4) is a male who was identified as an asymptomatic GATA2 carrier at the age of 6, following the diagnosis of P3 ... He was subsequently diagnosed with myelodysplastic neoplasm with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD), characterized by the acquisition of monosomy 7' (at age 8); 'To date, at age 11'. 'Patient #1 (P1) is a 75-year-old male without clinical features of GATA2 deficiency. Patient #2 (P2) is a 45-year-old male with deafness but no hematological manifestations.' Fig 1A genogram: P1 (father of P2 and P3) asymptomatic carrier; P2 deaf carrier; P3 immunodeficiency + vasculopathy + MDS-MLD; P4 (son of P2) MDS-MLD; P4's brother wild-type.
cases.notes: Proband taken as P3, the first diagnosed (P4 was tested 'following the diagnosis of P3'); relationships from the genogram (P1 = father, P2 = brother, P4 = brother's son, coded niece). The paper does not give an ACMG class; it presents the variant as the cause of GATA2 deficiency in the family. Proband's pancytopenia at 29 coded feature/bmf; MonoMAC with M. avium infection coded feature/gata2 at 31 (the paper text says 'monocytosis', probably an error for monocytopenia in MonoMAC; not resolved). Brother's deafness has no code; he and the father are unaffected carriers and are omitted. Proband's current age not stated.

'Their mother died in 2012 at the age of 74 of metastatic GIST. She presented with multifocal intestinal GIST ... Sequencing of tumor DNA revealed the same KIT N655K mutation'. 'In 2000, the maternal second-degree cousin of the index case (II-1 at pedigree) was diagnosed at the age of 59 with multiple gastric and small-bowel mesenchymal malignant neoplasms compatible with GIST ... cases.variant: 16,229 bp tandem duplication upstream of GREM1 including the 3' part of SCG5 (chr15:32,986,220-33,002,449, GRCh37), heterozygous; disease-causing per authors (increased GREM1 expression in colon mucosa)
cases.citation: Rohlin A et al. Genes Chromosomes Cancer 2016;55(1):95-106
cases.evidence: 'we have identified a duplication in the regulatory region of the GREM1 gene in a family with an attenuated/atypical polyposis syndrome ... The duplication of 16 kb in the regulatory region of GREM1 was found to be disease-causing in the family.' 'Family member IV:2 had follow-ups since the age of 21 and due to polyps a prophylactic IRA (ileo-rectal anastomosis) was performed at age 28. The histological examination showed one polyp in the rectum and six in the transverse colon'. 'Family member V:2 ... At the age of 25 coloscopy showed tubular and tubulovillous adenomas'. 'Family member III:2 had a colectomy at the age of 52 where histological examinations detected five polyps in the colon and a 4 cm polyp ... Metaplastic polyps in the rectum were also found on multiple follow-ups. Family member III:3 was operated for cancer in the transverse colon at the age of 33 ... 18 years later polyps in the left flexure and in the rectum were found and she had CRC at age 51. ... The sister of the twin sisters (III:4) was afflicted with breast cancer, their father (II:2) with gastric cancer and lymphosarcoma, and a cousin (III:6) with gastric cancer. A grandchild (V:8) had polyps (colectomy at 26 years of age) as had her mother (IV:6) (colectomy at 47 years of age) who also developed breast cancer at 61 years of age.
